ratings_why.fun: Lots of cards overlap: Berus killing Encore units, Anguis borrowing a Matron's scene, Coronella turning sales into scenes, and Old Crest and Hesketh deciding who should die last. That gives real slot choices every turn.
ratings_why.distinct: Encore is Reborn and the Prompter and Old Crest are a familiar deathrattle-multiplier stack. Understudy row-swapping and the cross-tribe Notices bank are what make it fresh.

verdict_why: The engine is good as it stands, but a few stacking and timing rules can't be read yet and need one pass to pin down.

points.text: Old Crest's replay is unclear: does the Prompter's Boy double a replayed scene, and does a unit that died twice (Encore) replay once or twice? Say which in the text.
Wreath-Bearer's Encore has no duration. Fired by the Rehearser or Coronella while recruiting, does it last into the next fight or end at once? Say 'this fight' or 'permanently'.
Prompter's Boy and Understudy share the back row: when Anguis steps into the front slot ahead of the Prompter, do his copied scenes count as 'in front' and fire twice? Write the answer down.
Notices only ever go up and get read as a total. One card that pays out on Notices gained this fight, such as a mid-fight buff at every 5th death, would turn the bank into an in-fight combo too.
Bit-Part Lizard could feed an Understudy behind it ('give a unit behind this +1/+1, twice if it has Understudy') so the Tier 1 seed points at the wings build.

standouts.why: Little Anguis copies whatever died in front of him, so the slot behind each lead becomes a real casting puzzle.
Old Crest makes you plan the order of death across the whole board, and he stacks with the Prompter and Hesketh.
The Brothers Berus use self-damage for a new job: they pop Encore units on purpose and give the bodies that get back up +4 Attack.

weakest.why: The Natterjack is a flat gold check that offers no decision once it's on the board.
The Bill-Poster just reads a counter, with no placement or timing hook.
Bit-Part Lizard gives one small buff to whoever stands behind it, and it fades fast.

flags.note: Hesketh's raise lets Old Crest die a second time and replay everything again, which on top of the Prompter could spiral. Worth a sim.
Encore deaths, Hesketh raises and Berus casualties all add Notices, so Žilvinas may grow far faster than 60 Notices on arrival suggests.
It's unclear how replays interact with the Prompter's doubling and with units that died twice.
The Encore it grants has no duration when it fires while recruiting.
